Latin word

auctiō

auctiō, auctiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

an auction; a sale by auction

In this lexicon

  • auction

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Men. 1157: Auctiō fīet Menaechmī māne sānē septimī; Cic. Att. 13.14: auctiōnis diem (Lewis & Short)

  • sale

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.3; Plaut. Men. 5.9.91–94 (Lewis & Short: auctiōnem facere)

Examples

  • Auctiō fīet Menaechmī māne sānē septimī. vēnībunt servī, supellex, fundī, aedēs, omnia. vēnībunt quīquī licēbunt, praesentī pecūniā.

    Menaechmus’s auction will be held bright and early on the seventh day. For sale: slaves, furniture, farms, house, everything. Sold at whatever they fetch, cash down.Plaut. Men. 1157–1159
